subject: Temporary GPU price buffer / credit path request for reserved commit
messages:
From: Amir Khan <amir.khan@terahealth.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Reserved capacity ask — short-term price buffer?

Hi Laura,

Thanks again for the walkthrough earlier. We want to move forward with the 9-month reserved capacity you quoted (estimated ~1.2M tokens/month footprint -> ~equivalent of a 4x A100 pool sizing), but we have a governance constraint: our procurement folks cannot approve multi-quarter expenses that have unbounded exposure to rapid GPU price inflation.

Two asks from our side:
- Can Redwood offer a short-term GPU price buffer / credit if the market GPU index (or your internal cost metric) increases more than 12% versus the baseline pricing at signing?
- Alternatively, can we structure a phased commit (3 months ramp + committed baseline thereafter) with a capped credit pool to cover spikes?

We'd prefer a declarative mechanism rather than multiple manual escalations — something that triggers automatically and is reconciled monthly.

Attaching our product roadmap and expected peak weeks for Q4. Happy to jump on a call with procurement next week (they’re in PST).

Best,
Amir Khan
VP Product, TeraHealth
Attachments: TeraHealth_Roadmap_Q4.pdf
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Wed, 30 Sep 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Reserved capacity ask — short-term price buffer?

Team — forwarding TeraHealth's procurement ask. Key points: they want either an automatic buffer/credit if GPU cost index spikes >12% or a phased commit with a capped credit pool. They plan to sign quickly if we can give a predictable, audit-able mechanism (monthly reconciliation).

Options I see (quick summary):
1) 6-month price buffer: Redwood provides a credit equal to variance above baseline up to X% (propose 12%) for first 6 months post-signing. Credits apply to invoice, reconciled monthly. Requires finance guardrails and a cap (recommend $75k total credit cap for this deal).
2) Phased commit: 3-month ramp then baseline commitment; exposure capped by staged commitment and usage look-back; simpler but delays full revenue recognition.
3) Indexed clause with trigger + audit: index tied to our published GPU cost index or cloud spot index; when trigger hit, automatically apply pre-agreed discount formula.

Requesting:
- Sean: are you comfortable with a $75k credit cap and 12% trigger as a standard for mid-market?
- Kimberly / Legal: can we produce a concise term snippet that is signable (2–3 sentences) and doesn't require enterprise counsel review?
- Karthik / Finance: what reporting/audit do you need to support automatic credits?

I attached a proposed_term_snippet.docx with draft language. I plan to respond to Amir with a provisional path (ask for internal approval) and request procurement meeting time.

—Laura
Laura Bennett
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Sep 2026 14:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Reserved capacity ask — short-term price buffer?

Thanks Laura. Quick thoughts:
- Approve route (1) but conservative caps: authorize up to $75k total credit as proposed, and a 12% trigger. That should be adequate to close and keeps our tail risk limited.
- Condition: credits must be reconciled against actual usage and only apply to overage/commit shortfalls, not to waive base committed spend.
- Escalation: if projected credit exposure > $500k (unlikely here), require VP Sales signoff + CFO notification.

Kimberly: please draft a two-line contract clause with the trigger definition, calculation method (simple formula), reconciliation cadence (monthly), and credit cap. Keep the clause opt-in for standard SOWs — enterprise counsel can review only if they request bespoke wording.

Karthik: you’ll need a monthly usage export (simple CSV) plus our internal GPU-cost-index monthly value. Can Finance own the reconciliation and apply credits to the next invoice? If not, propose an alternative.

Laura — once legal and finance confirm, send Amir a provisional term and schedule a procurement call. Aim to push this through in the week.

- Sean
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Amir Khan <amir.khan@terahealth.com>, contract-admin@terahealth.com
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 01 Oct 2026 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Reserved capacity ask — short-term price buffer? (provisional)

Hi Amir — thanks for the clear ask and for the roadmap doc. We can provisionally offer a short-term GPU price buffer per the terms below; final language will be added to the SOW and DocuSign packet.

Provisional terms (summary):
- Mechanism: Monthly reconciliation comparing baseline GPU-cost-index (baseline = index at signing) to actual index.
- Trigger: If index increases >12% in any reconciliation month, Redwood will apply a credit equal to the variance on that month’s invoiced variable usage, capped to a cumulative credit pool of $75,000 for the 6-month period following the effective date.
- Scope: Credits applied only to variable/overage charges; committed baseline spend remains billable.
- Reconciliation & audit: TeraHealth to accept monthly usage export and Redwood’s index report; either party may request a one-time audit within 60 days of a credit event.
- Expiration: Provision applies only to months within the first 6 months after signing.

Next steps:
1) We’ll attach the provisional term to SOW_draft_v2.pdf and send DocuSign link for countersign.
2) Procurement meeting: I’m available Mon/Tue morning PST; ping me a 30-min slot.

If this works, I’ll have Kimberly drop the two-line contract clause into the SOW and Karthik will confirm the reconciliation flow.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
